story: Mozilla and Microsoft are rebuilding their browsers’ foundations
text: If you have the time there is a nice talk about WebRender: [VIDEO] Here is another great talk: [LINK] At ~25:30 he'll also talk a bit about Quantum. In a nutshell WebRender is used to send a web page to the GPU which will paint all divs, borders, shadows, images etc. Currently WebRender is the only component I'm aware of that is inside Firefox Nightly. It's still behind a config though.

story: Transitioning Firefox's rendering engine from Gecko to Servo
text: >"If performance is not competitive" I don't think this will be a problem. One example... [VIDEO] [LINK]

You should take these advices with a grain of salt because it refers to the legacy rendering pipeline used by current web browers. There is not absolute rule stating that layout and painting must be slow while compositing is not. In fact Mozillians are currently working on a new rendering pipeline[1] based on state of the art rendering tools[2]. This new pipeline should be deployed in firefox in 2018 as a part of the ongoing Quantum project. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
I'm sure the future blog posts will have more details, but it has to do with immediate mode vs retained mode APIs. [VIDEO]
According to this: [VIDEO] Firefox's servo engine can compose CSS elements/Display List together at 500 frames / second. Maybe next version of Windows / Linux desktop should use FF's servo engine?
